channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Euractiv] EU Inc set to miss 2026 deadline as Parliament talks falter again
item.description: Lawmakers fail to find deal on workers’ rights for third time

item.title: [Euractiv] Finland, Estonia push Europe to compete in frontier AI
item.description: Countries urge to channel savings into funding tech growth ahead of AI meeting

item.title: [Euractiv] US envoys to meet Putin, Zelenskyy after war talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Zelenskyy welcomed a "change in tone" from the US on the prospect of Europe's inclusion in the Washington-mediated talks

item.title: [Financial Times] ExxonMobil launches legal challenge to EU carbon capture rules
item.description: US oil company invokes investment treaty to challenge Brussels’ green regulations and seek suspension of timing requirements

item.title: [Financial Times] Democrats pledge to expose ‘absolute avalanche of corruption’ under Trump
item.description: Congress member Jamie Raskin says he will launch sweeping probe of president and allies but warns party to avoid impeachment ‘distraction’

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘The only way to get this done’: Why the US wants Europe at Ukraine talks next time
item.description: The truth is, it was never just about Ukraine for Putin. Washington now understands this – and that’s both good for Europe, and potentially terrifying as well.

item.title: [EU Observer] The olive branch is a universal symbol of peace – but the West Bank’s autumn olive harvest is open season for Israeli settlers to pillage and kill
item.description: The olive has become much more than a household staple. In Palestine, the annual autumn harvest requires courage, protection by activists and an often deadly struggle. The contrast to Europe's olive tradition has never been so stark.

item.title: [Euractiv] EXCLUSIVE: Commission rebuffs Parliament on wastewater rules
item.description: MEP Oliver Schenk accuses the Commission of “regulatory stubbornness” over its refusal to revisit the rules

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lagarde would equal any other centrist in Elysée run, poll shows
item.description: The departing ECB president has previously ruled out running in next year's presidential election.

item.title: [Politico Europe] SONDAGE EXCLUSIF 2027. Christine Lagarde “bien accueillie” par les électeurs du centre
item.description: SONDAGE CLUSTER 17 x POLITICO. L'Institut Cluster 17 a testé le scénario d'une candidature à l'élection présidentielle de Christine Lagarde. La future ex-patronne de la BCE, que certains rêvent de voir entrer dans la course, fait d'ores et déjà jeu égal avec Edouard Philippe.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bomb threats hit hundreds of schools in Italy, Ireland and UK
item.description: Italian authorities said it was "likely a cyberattack" rather a "real threat."

item.title: [Euractiv] Spain probes TikTok over child sexual abuse material
item.description: Spanish minister calls for platform's suspension following damning investigation

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU needs a system to respond to AI incidents, Finland and Estonia say
item.description: In a letter seen by POLITICO, Finland and Estonia call for "EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents." This comes as European leaders are set to meet Friday to debate AI for the first time.

item.title: [Euractiv] Von der Leyen endorses Turkish push for global electrification goal
item.description: The European Commission chief stopped short of insisting that electrification must be 'clean'

item.title: [Euractiv] Germany must rein in debt-fuelled defence spending: experts
item.description: The top EU economy is pouring huge sums into bolstering its long-neglected armed forces to face a hostile Russia

item.title: [Financial Times] Thousands of schools in Italy, Scotland and Ireland receive bomb threats
item.description: Incidents appear to be latest co-ordinated attack aimed at disrupting life in Europe

item.title: [Euractiv] Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days afer shootings
item.description: The event is held each 11 November to commemorate the end in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria

item.title: [Euractiv] US envoys to meet Putin, Zelenskyy after war talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will first travel to Moscow

item.title: [Politico Europe] European gaming firms say new EU consumer rules will ‘cripple’ the industry
item.description: The EU's Digital Fairness Act clamps down on video-game practices where players are encouraged to spend real money to keep playing.

item.title: [DW] Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: [Euractiv] General strike over housing hits Spain ahead of election
item.description: Unions reported a 'massive' uptake in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012

item.title: [EU Observer] War of propaganda: Russia calls Ukraine a ‘burden’ and uses Moldova as a ‘testing ground’ to sabotage EU enlargement
item.description: From fake celebrity sex scandals to ominous warnings about land seizures and soaring bills, Kremlin-linked campaigns are working to turn ordinary voters against EU accession long before any referendum is held.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘I cannot be optimistic,’ says climatologist Jean Jouzel
item.description: Jean Jouzel, a renowned French climatologist, is not optimistic about the changing climate and the level of mitigation efforts. But he says people should should not give up on the fight against global warming.

item.title: [EU Observer] First talks about EU envoy on Ukraine war to dominate Dublin summits
item.description: Even a Nobel prize-winning expert, Geoffrey Hinton, who is known as the "Godfather of AI" for his work with Google, might struggle to hold the room's attention, as Europe debates how to handle the US-led latest push to end the Ukrainian war.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] New dark-pattern rules are ambitious and will take time to become EU law, professor says
item.description: As the European Commission unveils new rules policing tech companies and influencers, Christoph Busch tells EUobserver that the proposed Digital Fairness Act is ambitious and precise. The scholar warns it may take time for member states to agree on it.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia’s fake war maps at Abu Dhabi peace talks aren’t fooling anyone (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,721)
item.description: Delegates flew to Abu Dhabi hoping for a glimpse of compromise, but instead watched Russia double down on propaganda that leaves the endgame to this grinding war as murky as ever.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Systemic’ sexual misconduct in German armed forces, study finds
item.description: Some 40% of female soldiers and 20% of male soldiers said they had experienced at least one form of sexual misconduct in the past year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tino Chrupallas Alleingang
item.description: Ein Video über Donald Trump bringt Tino Chrupalla in der eigenen Partei massiv unter Druck. Weil der AfD-Chef die US-Migrationspolitik als zu hart kritisiert, erntet er offenen Widerspruch von Alice Weidel und einen Richtungsstreit in der Fraktion. Exklusive Einblicke in geleakte Austritts-Mails zeigen zudem, warum einst loyale Mitglieder der Partei frustriert den Rücken kehren. Die […]

item.title: [Euractiv] Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
item.description: Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland

item.title: [Euractiv] Hen cages could be scrapped by 2040, EU draft shows
item.description: The leaked regulation sets a 12-year phase-out for existing cages

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham promises 10-year plan before Christmas recess
item.description: The British prime minister says his blueprint will be presented to the Commons by Dec. 17.

item.title: [EU Observer] 81% of Slovaks back EU membership — so why is Fico trying to rewrite the 2003 accession vote?
item.description: Ján Mazák explains why rigging claims by Slovak prime minister Robert Fico show that the leader is either confused or intending to deceive people. The constitutional lawyer warns Ficos' disinformation about Slovakia's EU accession may be paving the way for an EU exit referendum in Slovakia.

item.title: [EU Observer] Consumers pay the price for online manipulation, and the EU Digital Fairness Act can put a stop to it
item.description: The EU's Digital Fairness Act (DFA) is one of the few initiatives of this legislative term through which Europe can improve people's lives by strengthening their consumer rights and helping them save money, write the Socialists & Democrats.

item.title: [Politico Europe] US to seek Putin’s ‘blessing’ for Europe to join Ukraine talks
item.description: After two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine have agreed a major prisoner swap, with final numbers to be confirmed, U.S. officials say.

item.title: [Euractiv] UN chief urges governments to tax Big Oil windfall profits
item.description: ‘Polluters must pay,’ says António Guterres

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine’s Zelenskyy welcomes US inclusion of Europe in peace talks
item.description: The talks in Abu Dhabi are the first between Russia, Ukraine, and the US since February

item.title: [Euractiv] EU unveils new rules to tackle online consumer harms
item.description: Brussels can fine Big Tech up to 6% of annual turnover for breaches

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How are EU countries performing in reducing their carbon emissions?
item.description: EU greenhouse gas emissions continue to fall, and clean technologies are expanding. That’s what the latest EU Climate Action Progress Report and the Carbon Market Report, published on Monday, show. Yet, progress is still needed to achieve the 2030 objectives.

item.title: [EU Observer] Two years on, Valencia is still demanding answers for 234 dead in the 2024 flooding – and blaming Sánchez rather than local Popular Party leaders
item.description: Two years on and with 234 dead, the people of Valencia are still waiting for answers as to why, with five days warning, flood alerts were not issued. If the forecasts were known, why did the local government delay a crisis response? And more importantly - who's to blame?

item.title: [EU Observer] EU‑UK carbon market deal close, with UK courting access to ‘Made in Europe’ before Dublin summit
item.description: A deal between the EU and UK on carbon emissions trading and carbon tax is imminent as British ministers push for sectoral agreements ahead of next week's EU-UK summit.

item.title: [Financial Times] Three cheers for an independent American judiciary
item.description: Strong rulings to protect electoral integrity helped pave the way for a peaceful and decisive midterm vote

item.title: [Financial Times] Inside Ken Griffin’s $5bn Miami takeover
item.description: The billionaire wanted to mould his ideal city — and found his clout went further in Florida

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [EU Observer] Best way to halt migration is to sabotage Europe’s economy – but nobody wants that, so what are the alternatives?
item.description: Keeping people impoverished abroad and destroying its economy are Europe's best tools to stop migration. Not even the most anti-migrant politician would seriously push for such a proposal.

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [EU Observer] Watchdog finds patchy customs controls leave big loopholes in EU’s Russia trade sanctions
item.description: Watchdog finds spotty oversight and unclear rules weaken EU trade sanctions with Russia. Calls on customs authorities and the European Commission to do a better job.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] From aid donor to ‘geopolitical actor’: EU’s Africa diplomat on upgrading security cooperation
item.description: The EU is advancing its role as a 'geopolitical actor' by accelerating defence and security talks with a series of African states. EUobserver talks to Patricia Llombart Cussac, the managing director for Africa for the European External Action Service, the EU’s diplomatic corps.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in Europe’ and low-carbon rules up for debate as EU eyes industrial law deal
item.description: EU deputy ambassadors meet on Wednesday to settle which countries count as 'European' and what may count as 'low carbon', as the Irish EU presidency races to strike a deal among member states before the end of the year.

item.title: [DW] Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
item.description: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

item.title: [DW] US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up Abu Dhabi talks with prisoner exchange
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia board to decide Jensen Huang’s fate after revelation of affair with subordinate
item.description: Head of US chip giant comes under mounting pressure days after claims he had affair with alleged Chinese spy

item.title: [Financial Times] Scott Colom wins historic Senate race in Mississippi
item.description: Democrat becomes the first Black person to represent the state since Reconstruction era

item.title: [Financial Times] Can India clean up Delhi’s deadly smog?
item.description: Residents ask why a country that can land a spacecraft on the Moon cannot prevent citizens in its capital choking on bad air

item.title: [DW] Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

item.title: [DW] Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

item.title: [DW] Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
item.description: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

item.title: [DW] New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

item.title: [DW] Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

item.title: [DW] EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

item.title: [DW] Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
item.description: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.
